title: Trump Signs EO 14248 Requiring Citizenship Proof to Register to Vote
description_short: Trump Signs EO 14248 Requiring Citizenship Proof to Register to Vote
description_medium: Trump signed Executive Order 14248 in March 2025 seeking documentary proof of citizenship for registration using the federal voting form. It also addressed voter-roll reviews, funding conditions, and ballot-receipt deadlines. The action raised disputes over presidential authority and election access; issuing the order did not by itself establish that every requirement became enforceable or survived court challenges.
description_long: On March 25, 2025, President Trump signed Executive Order 14248, Preserving and Protecting the Integrity of American Elections, requiring documentary proof of U.S. citizenship — such as a passport or REAL ID — to register to vote using the federal voter registration form. The order also directed DHS and DOGE to review state voter rolls against federal immigration databases, threatened to withhold federal election funding from non-compliant states, and ordered the DOJ to enforce Election Day ballot-receipt deadlines against 18 states that allow postmarked-by-Election-Day mail ballots. The Brennan Center estimated 21.3 million eligible citizens lacked ready access to qualifying documents. Federal courts repeatedly blocked the order's major provisions. U.S. District Judge Denise Casper permanently enjoined most of the order in June 2026, finding Trump lacked constitutional authority over election procedures reserved to Congress and the states. Colorado Secretary of State Jena Griswold called the order unlawful weaponization of federal power designed to make it harder for voters to push back at the ballot box.

description_long: In early April 2025, far-right activist and conspiracy theorist Laura Loomer visited the Oval Office and presented President Trump with a dossier accusing National Security Council staff of disloyalty to MAGA. Trump, furious, directed National Security Adviser Mike Waltz to fire them on the spot. At least 15 NSC officials were dismissed in the first wave—including senior directors overseeing intelligence, technology, and legislative affairs. By April 24, Reuters confirmed at least 20 firings total, leaving sections overseeing Latin America, legislative affairs, and international organizations largely unstaffed. Loomer, who has promoted QAnon-adjacent theories, openly took credit on social media. On May 23, 2025, a second mass termination swept the NSC as Secretary of State Marco Rubio (by then interim National Security Adviser) fired dozens more staff covering nearly every major geopolitical issue, from Ukraine to Kashmir. The administration aimed to shrink the NSC to just a few dozen people. Former national security officials described the gutting as catastrophic for institutional knowledge and America's ability to coordinate complex foreign policy responses.

description_long: In September 2025, Trump orchestrated the removal of U.S. Attorney Erik Siebert from the Eastern District of Virginia after Siebert, following a five-month investigation, concluded there was not sufficient evidence to charge former FBI Director James Comey. Trump publicly pressured Siebert to resign in an Oval Office address, then fired him when he refused to quit. Trump appointed Lindsey Halligan — a former personal attorney with no prosecutorial experience — as his replacement. Halligan was sworn in on September 22, 2025, and three days later secured a federal grand jury indictment against Comey on charges of making a false statement to Congress and obstructing a congressional proceeding related to 2020 testimony — just before the five-year statute of limitations expired on September 30. Halligan accomplished the indictment despite the full grand jury never reviewing the final indictment text; only the foreperson and one other juror saw it. Federal judges described the investigation as showing a disturbing pattern of profound investigative missteps and potential prosecutorial misconduct. On November 24, 2025, Judge Cameron Currie dismissed the indictment, ruling Halligan had been unlawfully appointed. The DOJ appealed. Comey had famously been fired by Trump during his first term while overseeing the Russia investigation.

The arrangement meant a sitting president's own publicly traded company was launching investment products in an asset class he was simultaneously regulating through executive appointments and crypto-friendly executive orders, creating an unprecedented feedback loop of personal enrichment and policy capture. Critics noted that Trump's deregulatory moves on crypto directly inflated the value of his own financial products while his administration dropped enforcement actions against crypto firms, including a pause in the SEC's fraud case against Justin Sun — who had invested $75 million in Trump's World Liberty Financial.

description_long: In early 2025, DOGE's mass federal workforce reductions systematically eliminated the staff responsible for processing Freedom of Information Act requests at multiple agencies, with the Office of Personnel Management responding to a CNN FOIA request for records about Elon Musk and DOGE's security clearances with the message Good luck with that — meaning the FOIA officers had been fired. title: Foreign Emoluments Corruption - Presidential Profiteering
description_medium: Trump retained ownership of businesses that received payments from foreign officials and other people seeking government decisions during his presidency. CREW documented conflicts involving those properties. The overlap raised constitutional and ethics concerns; payments and access should be distinguished from a final judicial determination that every transaction violated the Foreign Emoluments Clause.
description_long: Throughout his presidency, Donald Trump violated the Constitution's Foreign Emoluments Clause by accepting payments from foreign governments at his properties while making policy decisions that benefited those same countries. Foreign officials, diplomats, and business leaders stayed at Trump properties, attended events at Mar-a-Lago, and paid above-market rates at Trump International Hotel in Washington D.C., creating a direct financial relationship between foreign governments and the American president. The Trump International Hotel became what ethics experts called 'the locus of influence peddling' during his presidency, with foreign officials explicitly choosing to stay there to gain favor with Trump. Malaysian Prime Minister Najib Razak stayed at Trump International Hotel while under DOJ investigation, the Saudi government paid for approximately 500 nights at the hotel, and T-Mobile executives stayed there while seeking merger approval. Trump refused to divest from his businesses or place them in a blind trust, instead maintaining ownership while his sons ran daily operations, creating ongoing conflicts between his personal financial interests and presidential duties. The profits from foreign payments flowed directly to Trump through his continued ownership stake, making him financially dependent on foreign government approval. Air Force personnel were redirected to stay at Trump Turnberry in Scotland, forcing the military to pay Trump's business for government travel. The emoluments violations represented an unprecedented monetization of the presidency, where foreign policy decisions could be influenced by business relationships and where foreign governments could essentially bribe the president through legitimate business transactions.

title: Arlington Cemetery Desecration - Campaigning at Sacred Ground
description_short: Arlington Cemetery Desecration - Campaigning at Sacred Ground
description_medium: Trump's August 2024 visit to Arlington National Cemetery drew controversy over campaign photography in Section 60 and an encounter between campaign staff and a cemetery employee. description_long: Donald Trump violated federal law and desecrated Arlington National Cemetery by conducting a campaign photoshoot at Section 60, where recent war dead are buried, after cemetery officials explicitly denied permission for political activity at the sacred site. During the August 26, 2024 visit, Trump's campaign staff pushed aside and verbally abused a female cemetery official who tried to enforce federal regulations prohibiting political activities at military gravesites. The incident occurred when Trump posed for photos and videos at graves of service members killed in Afghanistan, despite being told such activities were illegal at the hallowed ground. Federal law explicitly prohibits political activities at Arlington National Cemetery, but Trump's campaign ignored these restrictions and physically confronted cemetery personnel who tried to uphold the rules. The cemetery official who was assaulted chose not to press charges because she feared retaliation and harassment from Trump supporters, highlighting the intimidation tactics used by his campaign. Trump's campaign later released a statement attacking the cemetery employee, calling her 'despicable' for trying to enforce federal law protecting the dignity of military graves. The desecration of Arlington Cemetery represented a new low in Trump's disrespect for military sacrifice, using graves of fallen service members as props for political gain while attacking those who tried to protect the sanctity of the nation's most sacred military burial ground. The incident demonstrated Trump's belief that no institution - not even Arlington National Cemetery - was off-limits for his political exploitation and his willingness to physically intimidate federal employees who tried to enforce the law.

title: Birthright Citizenship Executive Order Defies 14th Amendment
description_short: Birthright Citizenship Executive Order Defies 14th Amendment
description_medium: On January 20, 2025, his first day back in office, Trump signed Executive Order 14160 declaring that children born in the United States to parents unlawfully or temporarily present were not entitled to citizenship — directly contradicting the 14th Amendment's Citizenship Clause and 128 years of settled law since Wong Kim Ark (1898).
description_long: On January 20, 2025, his first day back in office, Trump signed Executive Order 14160 declaring that children born in the United States to parents unlawfully or temporarily present were not entitled to citizenship — directly contradicting the 14th Amendment's Citizenship Clause and 128 years of settled law since Wong Kim Ark (1898). Federal judges across the country immediately blocked enforcement. The Trump administration ultimately asked the Supreme Court to weigh in, framing it as a dispute over nationwide injunctions. In June 2026, the Supreme Court struck down the order 6-3 in Trump v. Barbara, with Chief Justice John Roberts writing that children born on American soil are citizens at birth. The order would have stripped citizenship from approximately 150,000 babies born annually in the U.S. Legal scholars called it the most direct unilateral assault on a constitutional provision in modern presidential history. Three justices — Alito, Gorsuch, and Thomas — would have upheld Trump's restrictions.
